# UI/UX Revelation Sweep — Discovery Breadth

The Awtsmoos renews every visible interface each instant; this notebook treats each screen as a vessel, not an excuse to redesign what already works. Awtsmoos.com is the field of manifestation: improve only where evidence reveals friction, breakage, clutter, inaccessible stacking, invalid layering, mobile failure, or confused interaction.

## Mission

Audit the complete `geelooy` surface across pages, apps, games, overlays, menus, dialogs, editors, dashboards, and responsive states. Preserve established working patterns. Repair only actual UI/UX defects and high-confidence structural risks.

## Evidence hierarchy

1. Runtime screenshots and DOM state.
2. Browser console and layout measurements.
3. Real route/component/style relationships in source.
4. Existing tests and documented behavior.
5. Static inference only when runtime proof is unavailable.

## Discovery categories

- Invalid or conflicting z-index / stacking contexts.
- Clipped dialogs, menus, tooltips, dropdowns, toasts, and HUDs.
- Mobile overflow, fixed-width layouts, unreachable controls, tiny targets.
- Excessive density, overlapping controls, unreadable contrast, cramped typography.
- Broken focus, tab order, missing visible focus, keyboard traps.
- Touch/hover mismatch and controls that depend on hover only.
- Viewport-height assumptions that fail on mobile browser chrome.
- Safe-area failures on notched devices.
- Scroll-lock failures and nested-scroll dead zones.
- Game HUDs that obscure play, status, or core controls.
- Responsive navigation failures and hidden actions.
- Inconsistent component spacing that materially harms comprehension.
- Modals exceeding viewport or lacking usable close paths.
- Canvas/game scaling that creates letterboxing, clipping, or unusable controls.
- Fixed-position elements fighting each other.
- Low-information clutter that blocks primary actions.

## Preserve-first rules

- No aesthetic redesign without a concrete issue.
- No public contract breakage.
- No broad global CSS rewrite unless a verified shared defect justifies it.
- Prefer local, reusable fixes at the correct abstraction boundary.
- Verify desktop and mobile after every affected surface.
- If a page is already coherent, leave it alone.

## Ideal-world possibilities

A perfect sweep could inventory every route, capture desktop/mobile screenshots, measure overlays, locate every stacking context, inspect every game HUD, detect horizontal overflow automatically, trace shared styles to consumers, and attach regression checks for every repaired defect.

## Reality boundary

The practical path is evidence-led sampling plus source-wide structural scanning: discover route/app/game universe, identify shared layout primitives and obvious anti-patterns, inspect suspect surfaces in browser, make bounded fixes, then regression-test affected families and shared primitives.

## Completion evidence

The work is complete only when the route/app/game inventory is covered, discovered real defects are fixed, modified source is re-read, relevant checks pass, runtime verification shows no regressions, and remaining high-confidence UI/UX work is empty or explicitly blocked by unavailable runtime paths.
